issues.t: Engine stalls from failing fuel pump (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may run rough, hesitate, fail to start, or stall while driving, sometimes with warning lights on the dash.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank used an impeller that can swell and stick, cutting fuel flow. Toyota and Lexus recalled many 2015-2019 RC models in two campaigns to replace the pump.
issues.next: Check your VIN at a Lexus dealer or nhtsa.gov/recalls. The pump replacement is free. If the car stumbles or stalls before the repair, don't keep driving it.

issues.t: Water pump leaking coolant
issues.sym: Pink coolant drips or crust at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, the coolant level dropping, or in bad cases a rising temperature gauge.
issues.why: The engine-driven water pump's internal seal wears and begins to seep through its weep hole. Lexus issued a bulletin on diagnosing non-electric water pump leaks across 2008-2021 models, and RC owners have reported pump failures around 50,000 miles.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and look for pink residue near the pump. Replace a leaking pump before it overheats the engine; check whether warranty coverage applies.

issues.t: Wheels can loosen if the wrong lug bolts or wheels are used
issues.sym: Vibration or a wobble from a wheel after tire or wheel work, which can lead to a wheel coming off.
issues.why: Some 2021-2024 Lexus models use hub bolts instead of studs and nuts. Lexus warned that mixing incompatible wheels, bolts or nuts can let a wheel come loose.
issues.next: Only fit wheels and lug hardware made for your car, and have them torqued by hand to spec. Stop driving and check the wheels if you feel a new vibration after tire work.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump can crack and leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; you might smell raw fuel around the car or see a wet spot under the engine.
issues.why: On RC F models, a pulsation damper on the two high-pressure fuel pumps can develop a fatigue crack under some driving conditions and leak fuel near hot engine parts, raising the risk of fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V107000 and have the free pump replacement done. If you smell fuel, park the car and have it towed rather than driven.

issues.t: Hard starting with lean check engine codes
issues.sym: The engine takes longer to start or doesn't catch on the first try, and the check engine light may come on with codes P0171, P0174 or P0087.
issues.why: Fuel pressure is too low, so the engine runs lean. Lexus issued a bulletin covering 2013-2020 models with a diagnosis and repair for this low-pressure condition.
issues.next: Have the codes read and fuel pressure tested. First make sure the fuel pump recall is done, since a weak pump causes the same codes.

issues.t: Brake vibration or grooved rotors
issues.sym: A shudder through the steering wheel or brake pedal when slowing, a squeak from the rear, or rotors with visible grooves at low mileage.
issues.why: Lexus bulletins point to lug nuts tightened unevenly (often with an impact gun) warping the front rotors, and to corrosion on the rear brakes. Owners have also reported grooved rotors early.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured for runout and thickness. Make sure lug nuts are torqued by hand to spec after any tire work.

issues.t: A/C blows the wrong temperature or from the wrong vents
issues.sym: Air comes out warmer or colder than set, changes temperature on its own, or comes out of the wrong vents with weak flow.
issues.why: Small servo motors inside the heater box that move the temperature and vent doors can fail. Lexus ran a customer support program (20LE01) for the servo motors and issued a bulletin for weak airflow and bad mode control.
issues.next: Ask a Lexus dealer if program 20LE01 covers your VIN. Otherwise a shop can test which servo has failed and replace it.

issues.t: 12-volt battery runs down when the car sits
issues.sym: Slow cranking or a dead battery after the car sits for a while, plus warning messages.
issues.why: Modern Lexus models draw small amounts of power while parked. Lexus issued a bulletin noting that storage time, temperature and this draw reduce battery performance and life.
issues.next: Drive the car regularly or use a battery maintainer if it sits. Have the battery tested if it struggles to crank.

issues.t: Check engine light with idle or throttle codes on the V8
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes such as P0505 (idle control) or P2111 (throttle stuck open); idle may be unsteady.
issues.why: Lexus issued bulletin L-SB-0032-25 for 5.0L V8 models including the 2015-2025 RC F. A redesigned throttle body and updated ventilation hoses address these codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a dealer whether bulletin L-SB-0032-25 applies. Don't ignore a throttle code; the car may go into reduced power.

issues.t: Front brakes squeal or squeak
issues.sym: A high-pitched squeal or squeak from the front wheels when braking, especially at low speed.
issues.why: Pad vibration against the rotor creates the noise. Lexus released bulletins with updated front pads for RC and GS models, both rear-drive F Sport and all-wheel drive.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether bulletins L-SB-0001-20 or L-SB-0034-18 apply. Updated pads usually cure it.

issues.t: Knocking noise from the vacuum pump at idle
issues.sym: A knocking or tapping sound from the engine bay at idle that can sound worrying.
issues.why: On the 3.5L V6 used in the RC 350 and RC 300 AWD, the engine-driven vacuum pump that supports the brake booster can knock. Lexus issued bulletin LSB006023 with a repair.
issues.next: Have the noise confirmed at a dealer and ask about bulletin LSB006023. It isn't usually a sign of engine damage, but check it rather than guessing.

issues.t: Clicking from front wheels on slow turns
issues.sym: A click or pop from the front wheel area when turning slowly, such as in parking lots, on rear-wheel-drive cars.
issues.why: Lexus traced the noise on some rear-drive RC models to front suspension parts and issued bulletins with a repair, first for non-F Sport cars and later for F Sport cars.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether bulletins L-SB-0011-16 or LSB001522 apply to your car.

issues.t: Navigation freezes, reboots or the screen acts up
issues.sym: The navigation or multimedia screen freezes, responds slowly, restarts on its own, or traffic info is missing.
issues.why: Software faults in the multimedia head unit. Lexus released bulletins with software updates for slow or frozen navigation and for the system rebooting.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the latest multimedia software update (bulletins L-SB-0035-15 and L-TT-0204-16).

issues.t: Bluetooth phone won't pair or keeps dropping
issues.sym: Your phone won't pair, connects only sometimes when you start the car, or call audio is poor.
issues.why: Phone software updates and head-unit software don't always agree. Lexus issued several bulletins on Bluetooth pairing and connection problems over the RC's life.
issues.next: Delete the phone from the car and the car from the phone, then pair again. If it keeps happening, ask a dealer for a head-unit update.

issues.t: Apple CarPlay drops out or the screen goes black
issues.sym: CarPlay stops working, disconnects, or shows a black screen; some cars show navigation glitches.
issues.why: Older audio and navigation software versions have bugs. Lexus released bulletins with updates for CarPlay dropouts and black screens.
issues.next: Try another USB cable first. If it continues, ask a dealer to update the audio unit software.

issues.t: Remote app and connected services stop working
issues.sym: The Lexus app can't lock, unlock or start the car remotely, can't be activated, or the SOS button and microphone don't work.
issues.why: The car's telematics module, its cellular connection or app settings can fail. Lexus issued several bulletins on remote app and telematics problems.
issues.next: Check that the car has cell coverage and your subscription is active. A dealer can test the telematics module.

issues.t: Musty or sour smell from the A/C
issues.sym: A musty, sour or mildew smell from the vents, often when the A/C first comes on.
issues.why: Moisture left on the A/C evaporator lets mold grow, and water getting into the car makes it worse. Lexus has bulletins on HVAC odors and on musty smells after water intrusion.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filter and check the floor for dampness. A shop can clean the evaporator; fix any water leak first.

issues.t: Water in the trunk from rear wheel arch sealer
issues.sym: Water in the trunk or spare tire area, damp carpet at the rear, or a musty smell after rain or washes.
issues.why: Sealer at the inner rear fender arch was applied improperly at the factory on some cars, letting water in. Lexus covered it with a campaign.
issues.next: Ask a Lexus dealer to check your VIN for the rear wheel arch sealer campaign. Dry the area quickly to prevent odor and corrosion.

issues.t: Check engine light with code P2610
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P2610 but the car drives normally.
issues.why: P2610 points to an internal timer fault in the engine computer. Lexus issued bulletin L-SB-0002-18 with a fix.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask a dealer about bulletin L-SB-0002-18.

issues.t: Seat stitching comes apart
issues.sym: Seams on the seats split or the stitching pulls loose, sometimes on very new cars.
issues.why: Owners of early RCs reported stitching separating on the seats.
issues.next: If the car is still under warranty, have the dealer document and repair it. An upholstery shop can restitch seams later.

issues.t: Check engine light with oxygen sensor code P013A
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P013A; the car usually drives normally.
issues.why: The rear oxygen sensor reports a slow response. Lexus issued a bulletin for this code.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask a dealer about bulletin L-TT-0311-22 before replacing the sensor.

issues.t: Tire label missing load capacity (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you would notice while driving. The tire and loading sticker on the door frame doesn't show how much weight the car can carry.
issues.why: Some 2020-2022 RC F cars left the factory with a tire information label missing the vehicle's weight capacity, so owners could overload the car without knowing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V615000 (Lexus 22LA03). The dealer replaces the label for free.

issues.t: Car pulls or drifts after tires are swapped around
issues.sym: The car drifts to one side on a straight road, often after tires were rotated, remounted or wheels refinished.
issues.why: The factory mounts tires as matched sets in specific positions to cancel out small differences that cause pull. Lexus bulletins explain that moving them can bring the pull back.
issues.next: Have the alignment checked, then try swapping the front tires side to side. Ask the shop to follow Lexus bulletins L-SB-0012-20 and LSB002922.
